The case is strong: The Spirits Business called the 10 a limited edition at its release, and in September 2024 the house withdrew its 11 and 14 and brought in a 13 and a 16 as the Heritage Collection with the 19 and the 30 (Whisky Magazine, Dramface, Wooden Cork). A record written for the 13 cannot lint until plan.json carries it (the name would lack 10), and this refuter may not touch plan.json. For the read-together agent, with plan.json: { "kind": "bottling", "key": "bladnoch", "from": "Bladnoch 10 Year Old", "to": "Bladnoch 13 Year Old", "why": "the 10 left the range and the house brought in the 13 as its first age statement in 2024", "agreed": true, "date": "2026-11-22" }, then the record rewritten for the 13, keeping the key and the card ids silence and founding: thirteen years in bourbon casks alone, 46.7% ABV, non chill filtered, with the producer's honey, citrus, cut grass and fresh apple; the silence card then asks when distilling stopped (2009) and why a thirteen-year-old of 2024 was distilled before the stop, which holds for any bottle distilled before 2017; the 10 moves out of others or stands as an older bottling.

No other swap proposed or needed; Auchentoshan's Double Cask carries every word of the roster's flagship, so its new name needs no swap, though the read-together agent may wish to write the roster's flagship as Auchentoshan 12 Year Old Double Cask.
